question: What should a networking outreach message include?

○​ Example outreach message “I came across your profile and, as a fellow [College]
            grad. I’d be thrilled to learn about your experience with [Role.] Any chance you
            have 10 minutes to chat next week? I'd love to get your advice!
  ●​ Networking question ideas
        ○​ It's great to connect with you via [Name] - thanks for making the time!

●​ Alumni tool
         ○​ Navigating: Search school name in search bar > Click on school > Click on
            “Alumni” tab on home page
         ○​ Filtering: Search alumni by desired function (e.g. “product manager”, be sure to
            use quotes). You can continue to filter by company
         ○​ Connecting: If you find someone with whom you want to connect and message,
            without using premium, select “Connect” button > Add personalized message
  ●​ Linkedin cold outreach message guidelines (Commonality, Curiosity, and Call-to-Action)
         ○​ Sentence #1: Prove you’re not a stranger, state what you have in common: “I’m a
            current/alumni of (school), and I was thrilled to come across your profile.”
         ○​ Sentence #2: State what you are looking for–learning, a referral, a job, etc: “I’m
            torn between a PM and consulting career path and would love to learn from your
            expertise.”
○​ Sentence #3: Take all the friction out of the process: “Any chance you have 10
            minutes for a quick Zoom chat?”

●​ Recommended read: The Two Hour Job Search
  ●​ Process for networking:
          ○​ 1) Generate a hypothesis to explore–industry, function, location, etc.
          ○​ 2) Generate learning targets–40-50 target companies and look at their earnings,
             strategy, etc.
          ○​ 3) Begin your networking list–people from undergrad and grad who work there
          ○​ 4) Plan first outreach
  ●​ Benefits of networking–refine target industry and roles, learn the vocabulary, identify
     hidden opportunities (60% of jobs are not posted,) practice and refine your personal
     pitch, and build relationships
          ○​ The further you are in your career, or after your MBA graduation date, the more
             likely your next job is going to come from your network
  ●​ Referrals
          ○​ Referrals come after you build the trusting relationship; start with a networking
             call, keep in touch with them, and then ask for the referral; never ask for a referral
             in the first call

answer: A networking outreach message should include elements such as proving you are not a stranger by stating what you have in common, such as being a current or alumni of a school [S2]. It should also state what you are looking for, like learning from someone's expertise [S2]. Finally, it should take all the friction out of the process by asking for a brief time commitment, such as 10 minutes for a quick Zoom chat [S2]. Outreach messages should also be short, under 100 words, and only ask for 15-20 minutes [S3]. Additionally, you should avoid mentioning looking for or asking for jobs or internships in the outreach message [S3].
